topics.label: Introduction and lecture objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture within the cancer course and sets out its learning objectives.

topics.label: Mutation and clonal evolution in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish how mutations can give cells an evolutionary advantage within conditions that permit cancer development.

topics.label: Environmental influences on cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the evidence that environmental exposures influence cancer risk rather than cancer being solely a matter of chance or inherited susceptibility.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections contribute to carcinogenesis, using Burkitt lymphoma as a detailed example.

topics.label: Environmental carcinogens and mechanisms of DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how environmental exposures generate DNA damage that can lead to cancer-driving mutations.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish mutational initiation from the promoter activity that enables initiated cells to proliferate and form tumours.

topics.label: Tissue and life-stage susceptibility to carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how biological context affects susceptibility to carcinogens and conclude with a recap that incorporates this specificity into the preceding mechanisms.

topics.label: Evidence and methods for assessing carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how carcinogenic effects can be identified and evaluated despite the limitations of available evidence and testing methods.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by summarising its conclusions and placing cancer risks within everyday risk–benefit decisions.
